_field_contract_.description: Academic contract defining how candidate Fields are observed, normalized, evidenced, and represented during BSD-to-Field generation.
instruction: Treat a Field as an academically or professionally recognizable knowledge domain rather than as a topic, technique, tool, job title, or arbitrary subdivision of a BSD.
Observe candidate Fields independently through all declared observers.
Preserve differences in terminology and granularity across observers before normalization.
Do not treat BSD naming or BSD membership as evidence of academic Field identity.
Normalize candidate expressions only when authoritative evidence supports a stable Field identity and semantic definition.
Require traceable provenance for every normalized Field and its adopted definition.
Use academic and professional provenance as complementary evidence where available.
Do not use model prior knowledge as provenance.
Allow the same Field to occur under multiple BSD observations without forcing exclusive BSD ownership.
Keep the normalized academic Field collection one-dimensional at this stage and do not infer parent-child, hierarchical, or nested academic topology.

a.description: Observe formal disciplinary and educational classification systems for recognized Field identities and boundaries.
a.focus: Discipline names, Field definitions, classification boundaries, inclusions, exclusions, and neighboring disciplinary identities.

b.description: Observe academic quality, accreditation, and curricular standards for independently defined Fields.
b.focus: Recognized disciplinary scope, curricular boundaries, expected bodies of knowledge, and educational identity.

c.description: Observe established scholarly and professional disciplinary bodies for recognized Fields and bodies of knowledge.
c.focus: Disciplinary identity, canonical terminology, bodies of knowledge, curricula, standards, and professional definitions.

d.description: Observe persistent research communities and scholarly infrastructures for evidence of stable academic Fields.
d.focus: Persistent research communities, publication ecosystems, conferences, journals, scholarly taxonomies, and research-area continuity.

e.description: Observe established academic institutions for independently instantiated disciplinary and program identities.
e.focus: Schools, departments, degree programs, majors, academic units, and persistent research areas.

f.description: Observe professional, engineering, occupational, and industrial practice for stable Field identities with applied recognition.
f.focus: Professional domains, engineering practice, occupational structures, industrial standards, and applied bodies of knowledge.
